newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Murdoch to extend tentacles to New Zealand pay-TV.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch to extend tentacles to New Zealand pay-TV.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's New Zealand news group, Independent Newspapers (INL), said Friday it was in talks to buy a substantial shareholding in the country's largest pay-TV operator, Sky Network TV.
Analysts said Murdoch, via his News Corp, was building another link in a global satellite pay-TV network.

By acquiring Sky in New Zealand with its 265,000 subscribers he would control another outlet for his huge investment in sports programming which he said on Tuesday he would use as "battering ram" for dominance in television markets.
"This is another brick in his global satellite pay-TV construction," said First NZ Capital equities analyst Guy Hallwright. "This is News Corp's big investment area."
Despite its name, Sky Network is not connected to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB.

As well as BSkyB, News Corp. controls Hong Kong based Asia-Middle East satellite channel Star TV, jointly owns Foxtel in Australia and has an interest in Latin American satellite network DHL. News Corp. also owns the Fox television network in the United States.
Murdoch plans to launch JSkyB in Japan later this year, which will supply 200 channels by next year and a similar joint venture next year in the United States, ASkyB.

Sky Network is currently half-owned by U.S.-based HKP Partnership, a group of powerful U.S. companies including Bell Atlantic, Ameritech, Time Warner and Tele-Communications Inc, which wishes to sell out.
That group earlier this year attempted to sell the Sky stake to Telecom Corp of New Zealand. The price was just under NZ$100 million ($70 million), an industry source said, but the deal failed.

One share analyst valued Sky Network at NZ$450 million ($315 million). Sky's recent deal to buy rights to screen rugby from Murdoch in rugby-mad New Zealand had greatly boosted subscriptions and revenue at Sky.

Murdoch in 1995 spent $550 million to buy the television rights to southern hemisphere rugby union in a 10-year deal. News Corp. has bought the rights to the National Football League (NFL) and English Premier League soccer, and has spent millions setting up a rebel rugby league competition in Australia.
